ev.section: BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions
ev.quote: # BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions

Proceedings of NAACL-HLT 2019, pages 2924–2936
Minneapolis, Minnesota, June 2 - June 7, 2019. c⃝2019 Association for Computational Linguistics

contribution.value: BoolQ is a reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions paired with Wikipedia passages, used to test inferential abilities of QA models.

ev.quote: We build a reading comprehension dataset, BoolQ, of such questions, and show that they are unexpectedly challenging. They often query for complex, non-factoid information, and require difficult entailment-like inference to solve.
to gather 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions into a dataset we call BoolQ (for Boolean Questions). Each question is paired with a paragraph from Wikipedia
Entailment: We consider two entailment datasets, *MultiNLI* [(Williams et al.,](#page-10-11) [2018)](#page-10-11) and *SNLI*
Entailment: We consider two entailment datasets, *MultiNLI* [(Williams et al.,](#page-10-11) [2018)](#page-10-11) and *SNLI* [(Bowman et al.,](#page-9-11) [2015)](#page-9-11).
Multiple-Choice QA: We use a multiple choice reading comprehension dataset, *RACE* [(Lai et al.,](#page-9-19) [2017)](#page-9-19)
First, we use the *QNLI* task from GLUE [(Wang](#page-10-3) [et al.,](#page-10-3) [2018)](#page-10-3), where the model must determine if a sentence from SQuAD 1.1
we also try building entailment-like training data from *SQuAD 2.0* [(Rajpurkar et al.,](#page-10-13) [2018)](#page-10-13).
Finally, we also experiment with leveraging the long-answer portion of NQ, where models must select a paragraph containing the answer to a question from a document.
Paraphrasing: We use the Quora Question Paraphrasing (*QQP*) dataset, which consists of pairs of questions labelled as being paraphrases or not.
Heuristic Yes/No: We attempt to heuristically construct a corpus of yes/no questions from the MS Marco corpus [(Nguyen et al.,](#page-9-7) [2016)](#page-9-7).

data_size.value: 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions: 9.4k train, 3.2k dev, 3.2k test (avg question 8.9 tokens, avg passage 108 tokens; 62.31% yes in train)

ev.quote: We split these questions into a 3.2k dev set, 3.2k test set, and 9.4k train set, ensuring questions from NQ are always in the train set. "Yes" answers are slightly more common (62.31% in the train set).

Our *Recurrent* model follows a standard recurrent plus attention architecture for text-pair classification [(Wang et al.,](#page-10-3) [2018)](#page-10-3). It embeds the premise/hypothesis text using fasttext word vectors
Our *Recurrent* *+**ELMo* model uses the language model from [Peters et al.](#page-9-6) [(2018)](#page-9-6) to provide contextualized embeddings to the baseline model
Our *OpenAI GPT* model fine-tunes the 12 layer 768 dimensional uni-directional transformer
Our *BERT**^(L)* model fine-tunes the 24 layer 1024 dimensional transformer from [Devlin et al.](#page-9-5) [(2018)](#page-9-5)
It achieves 80.4% accuracy compared to 90% accuracy of human annotators (and 62% majority-baseline)

We build a reading comprehension dataset, BoolQ, of such questions, and show that they are unexpectedly challenging.

strengths.value: Introduces a new dataset of 16k naturally occurring yes/no questions, paired with Wikipedia passages and used as a benchmark.

ev.quote: to gather 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions into a dataset we call BoolQ (for Boolean Questions). Each question is paired with a paragraph from Wikipedia

strengths.value: Shows yes/no questions require diverse inference: less than 40% can be solved by paraphrase detection alone.

ev.quote: Less than 40% of the examples can be solved by detecting paraphrases. Instead, many questions require making additional inferences

strengths.value: Finds MultiNLI transfer adds 3.5 points on top of BERT-Large pre-training, showing entailment data is complementary.

ev.quote: the additional gain of 3.5 points due to using MultiNLI is remarkable. This suggests MultiNLI contains signal orthogonal to what is found in BERT's unsupervised objectives.

strengths.value: Releases data and code publicly to enable reproducible benchmark results.

ev.quote: We present our data and code at [https://goo.gl/boolq](https://goo.gl/boolq).

weaknesses.value: Uses singly-annotated examples in train, dev, and test sets to keep the dataset large.

ev.quote: we elected to use singly-annotated examples in the training/dev/test sets in order to be able to gather a larger dataset.

weaknesses.value: Class imbalance: 62.31% of training answers are yes, complicating evaluation against majority baseline.

ev.quote: "Yes" answers are slightly more common (62.31% in the train set).

weaknesses.value: Authors note dataset has been updated since the inference analysis was done, so the type breakdown may be slightly out of date.

ev.quote: Note the dataset has been updated since we carried out this analysis, so it might be slighly out-of-date.

limitations.value: Each question is paired with one selected passage rather than a full document, which limits document-level reasoning study.

ev.quote: we only use questions that were marked as having a yes/no answer, and pair each question with the selected passage instead of the entire document.

limitations.value: Best model still trails human accuracy by about 10 points, leaving a significant gap for future work.

ev.quote: It achieves 80.4% accuracy compared to 90% accuracy of human annotators (and 62% majority-baseline), leaving a significant gap for future work.

limitations.value: Restricts questions to those whose first word is in a manual indicator-word list, possibly excluding rarer yes/no patterns.

ev.quote: we found selecting queries where the first word is in a manually constructed set of indicator words[3](#page-2-0) and are of sufficient length, to be effective.

future_work_stated.value: Build a document-level version of the BoolQ task to increase difficulty and end-user relevance.

ev.quote: Future work could include building a document-level version of this task, which would increase its difficulty and its correspondence to an end-user application.

future_work_stated.value: Pre-train models on several suggested datasets in succession or in a multi-task setup.

ev.quote: Note that it is possible to pre-train a model on several of the suggested datasets, either in succession or in a multi-task setup. We leave these experiments to future work.
